summary: Read-only multi-dimensional UI/UX + responsive + motion + a11y + RBAC audit of NU-AURA frontend, adversarially verified, synthesized into a prioritized remediation backlog
logs: Audit complete: 52 confirmed findings across 7 dimensions

backlog.title: 3-column grid without mobile fallback on BentoNavigation (attendance check-in stats)
backlog.detail: Line 672 uses `grid grid-cols-3 gap-6` to display Check-in, Check-out, and Hours stats without a mobile breakpoint. On 320px viewport, this creates a 3-column layout that exceeds the 320px width minus padding, causing horizontal squeeze and poor UX.
backlog.fix: Change `grid grid-cols-3 gap-6` to `grid grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 md:grid-cols-3 gap-4` to stack to 1 column on mobile, 2 on tablet, and 3 on desktop.
backlog.verifierReason: File /Users/fayaz.m/IdeaProjects/nulogic/nu-aura/frontend/app/attendance/page.tsx, line 672: `<div className="mt-8 grid grid-cols-3 gap-6">` applies a 3-column grid layout without any responsive breakpoints. The parent container (line 635) has `p-7 sm:p-9` padding. On a 320px mobile viewport, this leaves ~264px for content (320 - 56px padding), divided by 3 columns plus 24px gap-6 total = ~80px per column, causing horizontal squeeze and poor UX. This breaks the established pattern in the file (lines 325, 367, 424) which all use responsive classes like `grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-4`. The check-in/check-out/hours stats section needs mobile-first responsive columns.

backlog.title: 2-column form grid in modal without mobile breakpoint
backlog.detail: Line 216 uses `grid grid-cols-2 gap-4` inside a modal dialog (max-w-2xl) for Check In/Check Out time inputs. The modal is responsive and has `p-4` padding on mobile (line 92), but the 2-column grid inside doesn't respond to mobile width, causing the input fields to be cramped on 320px viewports.
backlog.fix: Change `grid grid-cols-2 gap-4` to `grid grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 gap-4` to stack inputs vertically on mobile.
backlog.verifierReason: Line 216 of /Users/fayaz.m/IdeaProjects/nulogic/nu-aura/frontend/app/attendance/regularization/_components/CreateRequestModal.tsx contains `<div className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-4">` without any responsive breakpoint. This forces a 2-column layout on all viewport sizes including mobile (320px). On mobile, the modal has effective width ~288px (320px - p-4 padding). With 2 columns and gap-4, each time input field receives only ~136px width, causing cramping. The modal constraint is line 95 (max-w-2xl w-full). Other modal forms in the codebase (CandidateFormModal.tsx:49, ProgramFormModal.tsx) use `grid grid-cols-1 gap-4 sm:grid-cols-2` pattern. The suggested fix (change to `grid grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 gap-4`) aligns with established NU-AURA responsive grid patterns and resolves the mobile layout issue.

backlog.verifierReason: Line 148 of /Users/fayaz.m/IdeaProjects/nulogic/nu-aura/frontend/app/attendance/regularization/_components/RequestTimeline.tsx shows: `<div className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-4 pt-2">`. backlog.title: Width property animated instead of transform (layout thrashing)
backlog.detail: The work progress bar animates `width` from 0 to a percentage value. Animating layout-bound properties like width, height, top, left causes layout recalculation on every frame, severely impacting performance. The exact code: `<motion.div initial={{width: 0}} animate={{width: `${workProgress}%`}} transition={{duration: 0.7, ease: EASE}} className={...} />`. This should use `scaleX` (a transform-based property) instead.
backlog.fix: Replace width animation with scaleX + origin: `initial={{scaleX: 0}} animate={{scaleX: 1}} style={{originX: 0}}` or use a clip-path-based approach. This keeps animation on the compositor thread and avoids layout shifts.
backlog.verifierReason: The code at /Users/fayaz.m/IdeaProjects/nulogic/nu-aura/frontend/app/attendance/page.tsx:705-707 definitively animates the `width` property: `initial={{width: 0}}` and `animate={{width: ${workProgress}%}}`. This violates the explicit constraint documented in /Users/fayaz.m/IdeaProjects/nulogic/nu-aura/frontend/lib/animation.ts:9-10 which states: "Compositor-friendly ONLY: variants animate opacity / y (transform) / scale (transform). Never width/height/top/left/margin/padding/font-size." The codebase has a correct example at /Users/fayaz.m/IdeaProjects/nulogic/nu-aura/frontend/app/fluence/blogs/[slug]/page.tsx:214 using scaleX with origin-left. This defect pattern is repeated in 4 files and causes genuine performance degradation through layout thrashing.

backlog.title: Hardcoded white text in bulk-select active state
backlog.detail: `.chipActive` and `.bulkbar` use `color: #fff` hardcoded. While this is intentional for on-accent text, the background is `var(--accent)` which changes between light mode (#2952A3) and dark mode (#6884dc). The white text on the darker dark-mode accent (#6884dc) may have insufficient contrast — WCAG AA requires 4.5:1 for normal text. Need to verify actual contrast ratio with the dark-mode accent value.
backlog.fix: Verify WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1) of white text on var(--accent) #6884dc in dark mode. If insufficient, use a theme-aware variable like `color: var(--text-inverse)` which is #ffffff in light mode and #0e1225 in dark mode, or use a lighter shade for dark mode: `.dark .chipActive { color: var(--text-1) }` if the light accent makes sense, or add a dark-mode-specific color.
backlog.verifierReason: Verified in /Users/fayaz.m/IdeaProjects/nulogic/nu-aura/frontend/app/employees/_components/employees-list.module.css:86 and 104. The CSS hardcodes `color: #fff` for text on `var(--accent)` background. In dark mode, var(--accent) resolves to #6884dc (from /Users/fayaz.m/IdeaProjects/nulogic/nu-aura/frontend/app/globals.css:346), creating a white-on-#6884dc contrast ratio of ~3.48:1. This fails WCAG AA requirement of 4.5:1 for normal text at 12.5px-13px. Affects .chipActive (line 82-86), .bulkbar (line 97-104), .bulkCount (line 108-110), and .bulkBtn (line 119-131).

backlog.title: Hardcoded white text on accent in bulk-select controls
backlog.detail: Lines 104, 127, 150 in employees-list.module.css all use `color: #fff` for text on `.bulkbar` (background: var(--accent)) and `.bulkBtn` (background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.12)). In dark mode, `--accent` is #6884dc (lighter than light mode #2952A3), and the semi-transparent white button background becomes hard to read against white text. The shadow separator at line 116 (`background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.25)`) also becomes invisible on dark surfaces.
backlog.fix: Replace hardcoded `#fff` with `var(--text-inverse)` or `var(--sidebar-text-active)` which are already defined for this purpose. For line 116 separator, use `background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.25)` only in light mode, and switch to `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.05)` in dark mode via a `.dark` rule or use `var(--sidebar-border)` which adapts to theme.
backlog.verifierReason: Verified in /Users/fayaz.m/IdeaProjects/nulogic/nu-aura/frontend/app/employees/_components/employees-list.module.css lines 104, 116, 127, 150. In light mode, hardcoded `#fff` text on `var(--accent: #2952A3)` is acceptable. In dark mode, the same hardcoded `#fff` is applied to `var(--accent: #6884dc)` (a lighter blue), creating poor contrast—white text on light blue. Additionally, line 116's `background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.25)` separator becomes nearly invisible on the light accent. The design tokens already define `--text-inverse` which correctly adapts: #ffffff in light mode, #0e1225 in dark mode (globals.css lines 187, 412). The bulkbar, bulkBtn, and bulkX elements need dark-mode-aware text and separator colors.

backlog.title: Hardcoded white thumb in Switch control
backlog.detail: The Switch thumb element uses `bg-white` (hardcoded) with `shadow-[0_1px_3px_rgba(0,0,0,0.3)]`. In dark mode, a white switch thumb against a light accent button (#6884dc from dark mode palette) is visually correct, but the hardcoded white string should use a token for consistency. More critically, the shadow is hardcoded to black (rgba(0,0,0,0.3)) which works in both modes but is not following the token system.
backlog.fix: Replace `bg-white` with `bg-[var(--text-inverse)]` (which equals #ffffff) to make it token-driven. The shadow can remain as is since a subtle black shadow works on both light and dark backgrounds, but consider using `shadow-[var(--sh-xs)]` for consistency with the design system if that shadow is acceptable.
backlog.verifierReason: Switch component at /Users/fayaz.m/IdeaProjects/nulogic/nu-aura/frontend/components/ui/Switch.tsx:50 uses hardcoded `bg-white` instead of the design token `--text-inverse` which is defined in globals.css (line 187 light: #ffffff, line 412 dark: #0e1225) and bridged to Tailwind (tailwind.config.js line 156). The hardcoded shadow `0_1px_3px_rgba(0,0,0,0.3)` also deviates from the token system (--sh-xs is defined at globals.css lines 121/381), though it functions correctly in both modes. This breaks design system consistency where tokens are the stated source of truth.

backlog.title: Non-Sky accent color (NULogic purple) applied to workflow status badge
backlog.detail: The OVERTIME workflow entity type uses `bg-nu-purple-100` and `text-nu-purple-700` (#8939A1 brand color), which violates the locked Studio Slate v2 accent system. Sky accent (var(--accent), #2952A3) is the single source of truth for interactive emphasis. The `--nu-purple` token is reserved for brand moments (logo, header) only, not functional UI.
backlog.fix: Change OVERTIME badge to use var(--accent-soft) and var(--accent-text) to match the design system's intent-named semantic palette. If a distinct visual is required to differentiate OVERTIME from other workflows, use a different semantic variable (e.g., status-info, status-warning) rather than brand colors.
backlog.verifierReason: The OVERTIME workflow entity type in /Users/fayaz.m/IdeaProjects/nulogic/nu-aura/frontend/app/workflows/page.tsx (lines 118-122) uses `bg-nu-purple-100 dark:bg-nu-purple-900/30` and `text-nu-purple-700 dark:text-nu-purple-300` as colors. According to the design system defined in app/globals.css (lines 40-156), `--nu-purple: #8939A1` is reserved for brand moments (logo, header) only, not functional UI. All other workflow entity types correctly use semantic intent-named tokens like `var(--accent-soft)`, `var(--warn-bg)`, `var(--ok-bg)` mapped to the Aura token system. The `nu-purple` color at line 239-244 in tailwind.config.js is explicitly defined as a NULogic brand color, violating the locked Studio Slate v2 design system where `--accent: #2952A3` is the single source of truth for interactive emphasis.

backlog.title: Chart accent token (#8b5cf6 — Tailwind violet-500) does not match Sky accent (#2952A3)
backlog.detail: The CSS token `--chart-accent: var(--chart-5); /* #8b5cf6 */` is assigned a Tailwind violet-500 hex, not the locked Sky accent. This causes charts (bar, line, pie) to use a purple tone instead of the unified blue accent, creating visual drift on dashboards and performance pages where charts are high-traffic surfaces.
backlog.fix: Change `--chart-5: #8b5cf6` to `--chart-5: var(--chart-1)` (the primary #2952A3 blue) or define a distinct, intentional palette if multiple chart colors are required by UX specs. Verify all recharts/d3 renders respect the token.
backlog.verifierReason:
The finding is REAL. In /Users/fayaz.m/IdeaProjects/nulogic/nu-aura/frontend/app/globals.css, the chart accent token exhibits a genuine design-system drift:

Line 106 defines the primary chart color: --chart-1: #2952A3 (Sky accent, the locked blue)
Line 110 defines the 5th chart color: --chart-5: #8b5cf6 (Tailwind violet-500, NOT the Sky accent)
Line 295 aliases: --chart-accent: var(--chart-5); /* #8b5cf6 */

This is confirmed in actual chart usage:
- /frontend/app/attendance/AttendanceWeeklyChart.tsx line 149 uses 'var(--chart-accent, var(--accent-primary))' for holiday bars
- /frontend/app/expenses/reports/ExpenseCharts.tsx lines 28-39 define a COLORS palette that includes var(--chart-accent) at index 6, which is used in PieChart rendering (line 96)

The problem: when charts render in high-traffic surfaces (expense pie charts, attendance bars, payroll dashboards), they use a purple accent (#8b5cf6) instead of the unified Sky accent (#2952A3). This breaks design-system consistency. The chart color is not an intentional secondary accent — it's a missed migration from a previous palette to the Aura design system.

Fix: Change line 110 from --chart-5: #8b5cf6 to --chart-5: #2952A3 (or use chart-1 directly), or if multiple chart colors are intentionally needed per UX specs, document and verify the design intent.

backlog.title: Employee table renders SkeletonTable during loading but no inline error for API failures within table
backlog.detail: Lines 533-541 show that when `loading` is true, a SkeletonTable renders. When the load completes and `visibleEmployees.length === 0`, an EmptyState is shown. However, if a query error occurs after the initial load (e.g., a re-sort or page change triggers a 500 error), the page shows neither the skeleton nor the empty state—instead, it renders the table structure with zero rows and no error message. The error banner (lines 428-433) is separate and may not be visible if the user scrolls past it.
backlog.fix: Add error state handling within the table rendering logic: before rendering `SkeletonTable`, check `if (error) return <ErrorBanner ... />;`. Or render a full-table error row/banner inline so the user immediately sees the failure without scrolling.
backlog.verifierReason: The code at /Users/fayaz.m/IdeaProjects/nulogic/nu-aura/frontend/app/employees/page.tsx lines 533-541 renders the employee table with a three-way conditional: if loading show skeleton, else if visibleEmployees is empty show empty state, else render table. However, when an API error occurs after initial load (e.g., on re-sort at line 346-357), the loading flag becomes false while visibleEmployees still contains old data and employeesError is truthy (line 132). The error banner at lines 428-433 displays, but the table below (lines 544+) still renders with stale data because the conditional at line 533 only checks loading and visibleEmployees.length, not the error state. This creates a UX defect where the user sees an error message separated from the problematic table rendering, and may not associate the error with the data displayed.

backlog.dimension: RBAC / Functional Correctness - Permission String Mismatch
backlog.title: Non-existent backend permissions used in frontend
backlog.detail: Frontend Permissions object defines EMPLOYEE_MANAGE ('EMPLOYEE:MANAGE') and EMPLOYEE_BANK_READ ('EMPLOYEE_BANK:READ') which do not exist in the backend Permission.java class. This causes permission checks to silently fail because the backend never seeds or recognizes these permission strings. Frontend pages like admin/employees/page.tsx (line 380) use hasPermission(Permissions.EMPLOYEE_MANAGE) to guard access, but since this permission is never checked by the backend, an unauthorized user could access protected endpoints if they bypass frontend permission gates.
backlog.fix: Either: (1) Add EMPLOYEE_MANAGE and EMPLOYEE_BANK:READ to backend Permission.java and seed them in the database, or (2) Replace frontend usage with existing backend permissions (e.g., use EMPLOYEE:VIEW_ALL for manage scope, or create a dedicated EMPLOYEE:UPDATE permission for bank data access). Audit all Permission constants in usePermissions.ts against backend Permission.java to ensure 1:1 mapping.
backlog.verifierReason: Verified in code: (1) /Users/fayaz.m/IdeaProjects/nulogic/nu-aura/frontend/lib/hooks/usePermissions.ts:20-21 define EMPLOYEE_MANAGE and EMPLOYEE_BANK_READ; (2) /Users/fayaz.m/IdeaProjects/nulogic/nu-aura/backend/src/main/java/com/nulogic/common/security/Permission.java contains no EMPLOYEE:MANAGE constant (grep confirmed); (3) /Users/fayaz.m/IdeaProjects/nulogic/nu-aura/backend/src/main/java/com/nulogic/api/employee/EmployeeController.java:250 explicitly states 'EMPLOYEE_MANAGE does not exist in the Permission registry'; (4) Backend uses FIELD:EMPLOYEE:BANK:VIEW (FieldPermission.java:14) but frontend expects EMPLOYEE_BANK:READ; (5) Frontend usage: app/admin/employees/page.tsx:380 and app/employees/[id]/page.tsx:703. Both permissions are undefined in backend, causing silent permission check failures.

backlog.dimension: RBAC / Functional Correctness - Missing Ownership Check on Direct-Object Route
backlog.title: Employee detail page calls GET /employees/{id} without IDOR protection on frontend side
backlog.detail: The page fetches employee data via useEmployee(employeeId) at line 209, which calls the backend GET /employees/{id} endpoint via employeeService.getEmployee(id) at frontend/lib/services/hrms/employee.service.ts:18-21. While the backend enforces scope checks via enforceEmployeeViewScope() in EmployeeController.java:181, the frontend does not validate ownership before rendering sensitive banking and tax data (displayed in the 'Profile' tab at lines 703-717). A user can directly navigate to /employees/{arbitrary-uuid}/edit or /employees/{arbitrary-uuid}/compensation and attempt to view/edit another employee's record. Although the backend will reject unauthorized requests, the frontend should prevent disclosure of the UUID form parameter and render an immediate access denied message.
backlog.fix: Add frontend-side scope validation: (1) Check user permissions and current employee ID before rendering the page, (2) If the requested employee ID is neither the current user nor within their scope (EMPLOYEE_VIEW_DEPARTMENT, EMPLOYEE_VIEW_TEAM), redirect to /employees immediately, (3) Do not render employee data until the backend response arrives and is verified as authorized. backlog.fix: Change default text color from `#000000` to `editor.getAttributes('textStyle').color || var(--text-1)` (or use the computed CSS variable value dynamically). For highlight, keep `#ffff00` as it is a functional color, but document that users should select appropriate contrast. Better: provide a sensible default based on the current theme, or let Tiptap track the user's last selection.

backlog.verifierReason: Confirmed in /Users/fayaz.m/IdeaProjects/nulogic/nu-aura/frontend/app/payroll/page.tsx lines 138-221. backlog.title: Add Employee form has no field-level error display for async validation failures
backlog.detail: The form uses react-hook-form with inline error rendering for validation errors (lines 775, 791, 809, etc.), but the form submission (lines 305-313) does not propagate backend validation errors or async failures back to individual fields. If the backend rejects the submission with field-specific errors (e.g., 'employeeCode already exists'), the error is only logged, not displayed in the form, leaving the user unaware of why the save failed.
backlog.fix: Catch mutation errors in the onSubmit handler and map backend errors back to form fields using `setError()` from react-hook-form: `catch (err) { const backendErrors = err.response?.data?.errors; Object.entries(backendErrors).forEach(([field, msg]) => setError(field, { message: msg })); }`.
backlog.verifierReason: The form submission handler at /Users/fayaz.m/IdeaProjects/nulogic/nu-aura/frontend/app/employees/page.tsx:309-312 catches errors but only logs them without calling setError() to propagate backend validation errors back to form fields. The createEmployeeMutation (useEmployees.ts:121-131) has no onError handler to map backend errors back to fields. Evidence: exact code at the cited lines shows only logging, not error propagation."

backlog.title: Leave page error aggregation masks individual query failures
backlog.detail: Lines 86-95 aggregate errors from three separate queries (balances, leave types, requests) into a single `error` variable. If one query fails (e.g., `balancesError`), the page renders a single error banner without indicating which query failed or what the user can still interact with. The other two queries' data may still be valid, but the error banner suggests a complete failure.
backlog.fix: Render granular error states for each section: `{balancesError && <ErrorBanner ... />}` above BalanceRings, `{typesError && <ErrorBanner ... />}` above the calendar, and `{requestsError && <ErrorBanner ... />}` above PendingRequests. This allows the user to see partial data even if one query fails.
backlog.verifierReason: The code at /Users/fayaz.m/IdeaProjects/nulogic/nu-aura/frontend/app/leave/page.tsx lines 86-95 aggregates three independent query errors (balancesError, requestsError, typesError) into a single error variable using a cascading ternary. When any one query fails, line 123 hides the entire content section with `{!error && (...)}`, preventing users from seeing partial data from queries that succeeded. For example, if balancesError occurs but requestsData is available, the leave calendar and pending requests sections are hidden even though they could render. The components (BalanceRings, PendingRequests, LeaveCalendar) all support loading and empty states, but they cannot be reached when error is truthy. The onRetry callback at line 119 only refetches balances, not the other queries. A proper fix would render granular error banners per section before each component.

backlog.title: Inline motion on table view fallback lacks transition timing
backlog.detail: The table view (fallback when not in grid mode) uses `<motion.div initial={{opacity: 0}} animate={{opacity: 1}}>` with no explicit transition. This renders instantly with no easing, creating visual popping when the view switches. While not a below-fold issue, it should respect the page's motion timing and ease curves.
backlog.fix: Add explicit transition: `transition={{duration: MOTION_DURATION.base, ease: MOTION_EASE.outExpo}}` or wrap in `<Reveal>` to use the foundation's defaults.
backlog.verifierReason: File: /Users/fayaz.m/IdeaProjects/nulogic/nu-aura/frontend/app/employees/directory/page.tsx, line 557. The table view container has `<motion.div initial={{opacity: 0}} animate={{opacity: 1}}>` with no explicit transition. While Framer Motion provides a default transition (not "instant" as claimed), there IS a real timing inconsistency: the container lacks explicit timing control while its child rows (line 586-590) have `transition={{delay: index * 0.03}}`.
